# Microsoft Q3 FY 2026 Earnings Show Cloud Growth, With Capacity Still Tight
Management focused on capacity expansion, agentic AI adoption, and a shift toward user plus usage pricing models.

## Microsoft Q3 FY 2026 Earnings Show Cloud Growth, With Capacity Still Tight
Azure remains the core constraint and the core proof point, with growth staying near expectations while peers show faster acceleration.

## Azure Capacity, Efficiency, and Hardware Stack Execution
Management described ongoing capacity constraints as the primary limiter on Azure growth, even as the company delivered earlier capacity in the quarter that enabled higher consumption. CEO Satya Nadella said Microsoft reduced dock-to-live times for new GPUs by nearly 20% since the beginning of the year and added another gigawatt of capacity in Q3 FY 2026. He also said Microsoft delivered a 40% improvement in inference throughput for its most used models across Copilot, tied to software and hardware optimization work. The company framed this as a multi-layer effort across data center design, silicon, systems software, and model optimization. Azure’s growth rate may remain a debate point, but execution on capacity conversion will decide whether the demand signals translate into sustained share gains.

## Guidance and Final Thoughts

# Micron’s Sold Out 2026 HBM And US$200b Bet On AI Demand
- The company states its entire 2026 HBM output is already committed under long term contracts.
- In response, Micron outlines about US$200b in planned capacity expansion to address what it describes as a historic memory supply crunch.

For Micron, having its 2026 high bandwidth memory output fully contracted and committing to about US$200b of new capacity marks a clear bet that AI focused demand for DRAM and HBM will stay tight for years.

### How This Fits Into The Micron Technology Narrative
- The contracted HBM supply and capacity build directly support the narrative that AI driven demand for advanced DRAM and HBM is creating stronger pricing power and a higher margin product mix.
- The article's focus on a historic supply crunch and US$200b of planned spend adds more color on how concentrated HBM capacity could shape future cycles, which is not fully captured in the broader discussion of DRAM and NAND volatility.

[![NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2027](https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/20224/6296531eb3aed3741918b6b5_DH1L4415-HDR-20220527-r5/DH1L4415-HDR-20220527-r5_mid.jpg?v=dba29dde-5a9b-4ac8-bf58-a0b78da89547)](https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/20224/DH1L4415-HDR-20220527-r5.jpg)

- Entered production with [NVIDIA Dynamo 1.0](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/dynamo-1-0), open source software that boosts generative and agentic inference on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs by up to 7x, with widespread global adoption.
